# Draft:Wyn Thomas (historian)

Wyn Thomas (born 3 November 1967), also known as Dr. Wyn Thomas, is a Welsh historian, author, and musician from Llandrindod Wells, Powys. He is known for his works on Welsh political protest, particularly regarding the flooding of Cwm Tryweryn and the protests surrounding the 1969 Royal Investiture. He has published three books and released two albums as a singer-songwriter.
Early life and education
Thomas was born in Llandrindod Wells, the son of a policeman. He spent part of his childhood in Ammanford and Ystradgynlais before the family returned to Llandrindod Wells in 1977. He attended Llandrindod High School and Coleg Powys.
He obtained his first degree in 2001 from the University of Wales. His Ph.D. thesis, titled Wales and Militancy 1952–1970, was completed at Swansea University in 2011.
Career
Writing and academia
Thomas has published three books on Welsh political history, all published by Y Lolfa:
* Hands Off Wales – Nationhood and Militancy (first published 2013 by Gwasg Gomer; republished 2022 by Y Lolfa)
* John Jenkins: The Reluctant Revolutionary? (2019)
* Tryweryn: A New Dawn? The Legacy of the Drowning of Capel Celyn (2023)
A review in Nation.Cymru described Hands Off Wales as a work built on extensive research and interviews with those involved in the militant campaigns and those tasked with stopping them.
Thomas has presented lectures at the North American Festival of Wales (NAFoW) in Pittsburgh (2024), at universities including the University of St Andrews, and for organisations including The Honourable Society of Cymmrodorion in London.
Thomas is a former history tutor at Swansea University. In 2022–2023, he was employed as a consultant for the Welsh Government in relation to the Welsh education history syllabus, working on a resource concerning the contributions of black, Asian, and ethnic minority people to Welsh life, which was introduced in Welsh schools in September 2023.
Television
Thomas has acted as historical consultant and lead interviewee on several television productions. The Prince and the Bomber (BBC), directed by Marc Evans, won the BAFTA Cymru award for Single Documentary at the 2020 British Academy Cymru Awards. The production company Telesgop credited Thomas as "author and historian" on the documentary.
Other television credits include ''Y Bomiwr a'r Tywysog (BBC/S4C), Wales: England's Colony? (BBC), Wales This Week: Under Fire (ITV), and A Plot to Kill the Prince? (ITV).
In 2015, Thomas wrote and presented Tryweryn: 50 Years On for the BBC.
Radio and podcasts
Thomas has served as historical consultant on radio productions including God Bless the Prince of Wales (BBC Radio 4), A Nation Torn: Wales' Summer of '69 (BBC Radio Wales), Protest Nation (BBC Radio Wales), and Tryweryn (BBC Radio Cymru).
He has contributed to The World at One (BBC Radio 4) and The History Show (RTÉ).
Thomas was the historical consultant on the podcast Drowned – The Flooding of a Village (BBC Wales), presented by Betsan Powys, which aired in spring 2023. Drowned won the Audio News and Current Affairs Programme of the Year at the Wales Media Awards in November 2023.
Music
Thomas is a singer-songwriter who plays acoustic and electric guitar, 12-string guitar, harmonica, and keyboards. He released the folk and folk/rock album Chalybeate Spring in 2017 and Orion's Belt'' in 2022.
Musicians who have collaborated with Thomas include Geoff Downes (keyboardist with The Buggles, Yes and Asia), Aled Richards (drummer with Catatonia), Andrew 'Wal' Coughlan (bass player with Gary Numan, Alison Moyet, Martha Reeves and Shakin' Stevens), and Pete Hurley and Jane Williams (both of whom have performed with Van Morrison).
Thomas fronts the folk/rock band The Barefoot Rascals.
Personal life
Thomas married his partner Susie in 2004. He has two daughters.
